questions.question: The three steps of the rendering pipeline are:
questions.explanation: Changing a property can trigger layout (reflow), paint, and/or composite. Fewer stages = better performance.

questions.question: Animating transform/opacity is cheap because they:

options.text: Only trigger compositing (GPU), skipping layout and paint

questions.explanation: transform/opacity are compositor-only properties — the browser promotes the layer and animates on the GPU without reflow/paint.

questions.question: Animating 'width' or 'top' is expensive because it:

options.text: Triggers layout (reflow) which can affect the whole document

questions.explanation: Geometry changes force layout recalculation and often repaint — costly, especially with many elements. Prefer transform.

questions.question: Containment (contain: layout paint) helps by:

options.text: Isolating a subtree so its changes don't reflow/paint the whole page

questions.explanation: contain hints the browser to limit the scope of layout/paint work, improving performance for complex/animated components.

questions.question: will-change should be used:

options.text: Sparingly, only before an expected change, and removed after

questions.explanation: will-change reserves memory/layers; overuse bloats memory and can hurt. Apply just-in-time, not globally.

questions.question: The '60fps' target exists because:

options.text: Most displays refresh ~60 times/sec; hitting it avoids jank

questions.explanation: Smooth animation needs ~16ms per frame. Dropping frames (jank) feels laggy; keep work off the main thread where possible.

questions.question: A long task on the main thread causes:
questions.explanation: Heavy JS/layout work blocks the main thread, starving animation/input — minimize and break up long tasks.

questions.question: prefers-reduced-motion benefits performance AND:
questions.explanation: Reducing motion is primarily an a11y win, and disabling heavy animation also saves battery/CPU.
